question: Does a law tuned to the compression-stiffening endpoint stay mathematically admissible in the other loading modes a grasping task visits?

criteria.drucker: min eigenvalue of the 6x6 dS/dE material tangent > 0
criteria.strong_ellipticity: min over unit n of the smallest eigenvalue of the acoustic tensor Q(n)_ik = A_iJkL n_J n_L > 0; 400 Fibonacci directions
criteria.monotonicity: dP11/dlambda > 0 along the free-lateral uniaxial path
criteria.normalisation: every law carries unit small-strain shear modulus, so the eigenvalues are dimensionless multiples of G0

limitations: Material-point analysis. Admissibility here is necessary, not sufficient, for a stable discretisation: element quality, volumetric locking and time-integration stability are untouched.
Purely hyperelastic. No rate dependence, relaxation or hysteresis, while the calibration endpoint came from an oscillatory viscoelastic measurement.
Strong ellipticity is sampled over a finite set of directions, so a narrow violation cone could be missed between samples.
Tangents come from central differences of the analytic stress, not closed-form fourth-order derivatives; eigenvalues near zero carry the differencing error.
No parameter here is identified or promoted. The deformation ranges are plausible handling envelopes, not measured task trajectories.
